The within-firm timing dimension is a genuinely different economic claim from the archive's cross-sectional quality partners, the expression matches the hypothesis and sign, though TS_RANK over only five annual observations is coarse and the signal risks collapsing into a known earnings-momentum effect interacted with R&D intensity.

Maturity mismatch against long-duration intangible projects is an economically distinct and internally consistent claim, and the construction cleanly decomposes the earlier runway result, but the short-term-debt/rollover-risk channel is close to published debt-maturity return evidence so the incremental novelty rests entirely on the R&D interaction.

A defensible downside-quality reframing of the archive's restated-profitability ratio, but it is the same construct with MA(·,3) swapped for TS_MIN(·,5) and will be very highly correlated with IntangibleCapitalizedProfitability, so the incremental information content is likely thin and it risks being scored as an operator-level variant rather than a new mechanism.

This is SustainedResearchFloorCashBacked with oancf replaced by ib+dp — a proxy substitution that the reasoning itself frames as a coverage diagnostic, and since ib+dp is near-collinear with operating cash flow at annual frequency it is a cosmetic variant of an already-evaluated signal rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

TS_MIN(xrd/at,5) is empirically almost the same variable as xrd/at, so this is effectively a near-duplicate of the archive's InnovatorLowRolloverBurden, and the short-term-debt leg is a well-known low-leverage/distress sort providing little incremental mechanism beyond a mechanical leg swap between two existing signals.

Broadening the validation denominator from acquired to total (acquired plus internally accumulated) intangible capital is an economically coherent generalization that should roughly double breadth on the archive's best-balanced ratio, though the denominator collapses toward zero for low-intangible firms and the winsorized rank should be checked for whether it degenerates into a plain cash-flow-to-capital profitability sort.

The sign logic is internally consistent (deep loss trough plus a heavy intangible book predicts low returns) and the impairment-trigger framing is more specific than the earlier coverage leg, but the trough-earnings leg is largely the well-documented loss-firm/profitability effect, so the signal must be shown to add something beyond a distress sort interacted with intangible intensity.

The within-firm peak-normalized research intensity is a genuinely different, scale-free retrenchment measure that the archive has not tested and is not simply another cross-sectional level sort, though it partially overlaps the known R&D-change literature, will be undefined/zero for firms without R&D, and may have little dispersion since most continuous spenders sit near their own five-year max.

TS_MIN of a pointwise MIN is algebraically identical to MIN of the two separate five-year troughs, so the advertised "within-year binding constraint" novelty is illusory and the signal reduces to a re-blend of InternallyFundedRnDFloor and TroughCashFlowInnovator, with the added defect that COALESCE(xrd,0) piles all non-R&D firms at exactly zero while loss-year firms fall below them, so the cross-section is driven by cash-flow distress rather than by research capacity.

A defensible conjunction of two independently strong archive legs whose information sets differ (five-year policy floor vs. contemporaneous restated return), though the two legs share the xrd stock and the IND_RANK-product form is by now the project's default template, so expected incremental content is modest.

R&D stock scaled by liabilities is essentially the product of two long-published effects (R&D intensity and low leverage) with no interaction beyond division, and because COALESCE(xrd,0) forces the numerator to zero for the majority of firms the industry rank collapses into a large tie block that mostly re-sorts on nothing.

Economically coherent impairment-trigger story, but it is a one-operator substitution (MA→TS_MIN) on the identical two legs of IntangibleBookWeakDebtCoverage — a cosmetic refinement of an already-tested signal rather than new content, and the trough of oancf/lt is close to a standard distress screen.

The move from a one-year leverage delta to a five-year liability-share trend is a substantive rather than cosmetic repair of SelfFinancedRnDExpansion and adds a financing-policy dimension absent from the best commitment signal, though the deleveraging leg overlaps with the well-known net-external-financing anomaly.

The stated diagnosis is selective and inconsistent with the archive — CapitalLightKnowledgeFranchise actually produced a correctly signed FF5 alpha (+2.0%, t=2.43) alongside its wrong-signed slope — so this is a bare sign flip of a mixed-evidence signal, and asserting a positive premium for high dp/at directly contradicts the established investment/asset-intensity effect without any new identifying content.

The two "certifications" (MA(oancf/at) and NEG(MA((ib−oancf)/at))) are both monotone increasing in operating cash flow and therefore highly correlated, so MIN of their ranks will largely reproduce either archived signal (both already ~4.7% alpha) rather than test genuine complementarity — a near-cosmetic recombination of two existing results.

Research efficiency (ib per dollar of accumulated R&D) is a certification leg the archive has not tried, but note the mechanical tension that the yield leg is decreasing in R&D stock while the commitment leg is increasing in R&D intensity, so partial cancellation and heavy clustering of non-reporters at zero are real risks.

The expression and expected negative sign are internally consistent and the design sensibly conjoins the archive's strongest short-side slope with its strongest short-side alpha, but with re/at and oancf/lt as the two ingredients it risks collapsing into a generic financial-distress composite (a well-documented anomaly) rather than a purchase-accounting-specific effect.

This addresses a genuine open design question (within-firm versus cross-sectional measurement of research commitment) with a construction fix that removes the degenerate TS_MAX denominator that crippled the earlier 4% coverage variant, though TS_RANK over five annual observations is coarse and degenerate for non-R&D firms.

Economically coherent and the ib-based restatement plausibly lifts coverage above the oancf-constrained leader, but it is the third conjunction built on the same commitment-floor leg and the restated-profitability leg itself embeds R&D intensity, so incremental information over existing family members may be small.

This is a single-input numerator swap (oancf → ib) on an already-tested validation ratio family, and cross-sectional variation in the ratio is likely dominated by the inverse of intangible intensity in the denominator, so the coverage gain does not clearly justify it as a substantively different test.

The weakest-link certification is internally consistent with the stated hypothesis and pairs two legs whose archive evidence appeared on different metrics (cash-flow leg on the FMB slope, maturity leg on alpha), so it is a substantive rather than cosmetic extension of SustainedResearchFloorCashBacked — though it inherits that signal's ~9% coverage and must beat its already-strong 0.445 Sharpe to be informative.

Structurally identical to the preceding proposal with net working capital replacing near-term maturities, and the two certifications it MINs (operating cash flow and net working capital) are much more economically correlated than the cash/maturity pair, so the "clean design test" framing is fair but the incremental information content is thin.

Obligation-scaled profitability is an untested normalization with a genuine coverage gain, but ib/lt is close to a mechanical product of ROA and inverse leverage — both already represented in the archive — and the unwinsorized ratio will be dominated by low-liability firms even after IND_RANK.

A clean, internally consistent continuous variable that fills the untested 2x2 cell (trough evaluation × current-asset-excluded denominator), but the outcome is largely predictable from the two archived legs and the five-year minimum of a restated ROA is in practice a "never had a loss year" screen, which overlaps existing profitability/loss-persistence effects.

This reuses the exact ingredients of gen-7's UnearnedIntangibleBookWeakCoverage (goodwill/intangible book, oancf/lt coverage, retained earnings) with only the aggregation changed from additive to MIN, so it is a cosmetic reconfiguration, and low retained earnings plus weak cash coverage is a well-known distress/O-score composite rather than an acquisition-accounting mechanism.

This is the first dynamic (growth-race) certification paired with the research-commitment floor rather than another level-of-quality leg, and the sign logic is coherent; the main construction risk is that GROWTH of a three-year cumulative cash flow is ill-behaved when the base crosses zero, which could inject sign-flipping noise into the certification rank.

This is essentially the gen-8 flagship CommitmentWithCashOutpacingIntangibleGrowth with GROWTH swapped for TREND — a construction tweak rather than new economics — and because the SUB of two unstandardized trends is dominated by the far more variable intangible-intensity leg, the signal risks collapsing into a rediscovery of the intangible/asset-growth anomaly rather than testing a cash-versus-intangible "race."

Mechanically coherent and sign-consistent, but it is a three-leg stack assembled by picking the archive's best-performing legs ex post (commitment floor × validation race × low dlc) with no genuinely new mechanism, and it inherits the 6.6% coverage the objective explicitly warns about, so any "dominance over both parents" is very likely selection noise.

Substituting ib for oancf is derivative of the same race construction, but the near-doubling of sample and the explicit cash-versus-accrual diagnostic give it real informational value, subject to the same caveat that the unscaled trend difference may be driven mainly by the intangible-base leg (i.e., intangible growth).

A legitimately new pairing of two individually validated but informationally distinct legs on the wider-coverage restatement channel, with matching sign logic; the main risk is that the low-short-term-debt leg is a repackaging of known distress/maturity-structure effects and may carry most of the alpha, which the test should diagnose by reporting the leg-only benchmark.

The MAX ("worse of two channels") aggregator is a genuine structural innovation on the under-explored short side, orientations are consistently signed for the negative expected sign, and it adds maturity structure that no prior intangible-fragility signal used — though MAX will also assign full fragility to cash-rich firms with merely short-dated debt, which could dilute the prior coverage-based result.

A derivative reshuffle of two already-archived legs into the gen-8 weakest-link form, but the 60% coverage expansion makes it a defensible robustness test of whether the effect is a post-1988 cash-flow-statement artifact; note that ib/lt is close to a standard profitability-and-leverage composite, so incremental information over known quality anomalies should be checked.
